recentItems.title: Lul Tim Reacts to Lil Durk's Murder-for-Hire Arrest for Killing His Friend Lul Pab (Flashback)
recentItems.description:
In this flashback, Lul Tim weighed in on the high-profile arrest of Lil Durk and five others in connection with an alleged murder-for-hire plot that resulted in the killing of Lul Pab. According to federal prosecutors, the alleged operation involved suspects traveling from Chicago to San Diego, as well as a private flight from Miami to Los Angeles, with funding allegedly tied to Lil Durk.

The indictment detailed an elaborate series of arrangements involving flights, accommodations, rental vehicles, and the alleged purchase of weapons. However, prosecutors say the plot ultimately resulted in the killing of the wrong person, with Lul Pab being fatally shot at a gas station.

Lul Tim criticized the alleged operation as "sloppy work," pointing to the extensive paper trail left behind by those involved. Amid the public controversy and online reactions, Tim reflected on the bigger picture, arguing that the situation illustrates the destructive cycle of violence, retaliation, and legal trouble that continues to affect the hip-hop community.

recentItems.title: DJ Vlad Reacts to Keefe D Found Guilty for Killing 2Pac
recentItems.description:

--------
DJ Vlad breaks down the Nevada murder verdict against Duane “Keefe D” Davis in the long-running 2Pac case, after a Las Vegas jury deliberated for just 90 minutes before finding him guilty of first-degree murder with a deadly weapon. Vlad explains why he is not celebrating the conviction, discusses Las Vegas PD’s attempts to obtain VladTV raw footage, and reflects on how Keefe D’s book and interviews became central to the trial.

The commentary revisits key names tied to the case, including Tupac Shakur, Orlando Anderson, the Southside Crips, Mob James, E.D.I. Mean of the Outlawz, Reggie Wright Jr., Greg Kading, Zip, Foxy Brown, and Judge Mathis. Vlad also addresses the BET hot mic issue, Keefe D’s rejected plea deal, possible appeal, sentencing, and why speaking publicly about a decades-old murder may have changed the outcome forever.

recentItems.title: FBG Butta Predicted Lil Durk Would Be Arrested for M***** for Hire (Flashback)
recentItems.description:
In this flashback, FBG Butta questioned why Lil Durk was still free despite his name allegedly being implicated in various instances of criminal activity. Butta specifically referenced allegations that Durk had paid for assassinations and suggested that his wealth and legal representation may have helped him avoid incarceration.

At the time, Butta’s comments came months before Lil Durk was arrested on federal murder-for-hire charges stemming from an alleged plot targeting Quando Rondo. Prosecutors allege that the 2022 shooting resulted in the death of Rondo’s cousin and close associate, Saviay’a “Lul Pab” Robinson, while Rondo survived. Durk has pleaded not guilty and denies the allegations.

Judge Mathis joins VladTV to discuss his personal connection to Lil Durk as the rapper’s trial nears a possible conclusion, revealing Durk once asked him to officiate his wedding in India. Mathis reflects on Durk’s efforts to move in a positive direction, including plans to visit the Mathis Community Center in Detroit, the success of “All My Life” featuring J. The conversation turns to OTF Jam, aka Jamie the Bull, whose cooperation stunned Mathis given the “gang politics” and street code surrounding testimony. Vlad compares the situation to insights from Brian “Glaze” Gibbs, while Mathis explains how long sentences changed cooperation in criminal cases. The interview also touches on Detroit hitman Nate “Boone” Craft, known as the Grim Reaper, and the harsh realities behind loyalty, violence, and federal deals.

Hit-Boy joins DJ Vlad for a sharp hip-hop debate on artistry, talent, and legacy, weighing the creative differences between Jay-Z and Kanye West. The producer reflects on Kanye’s electrifying studio energy and genre-bending instincts, while also sharing a memorable 2013 moment when Jay-Z delivered an a cappella verse during sessions around a Beyoncé album, leaving him stunned by Hov’s pure rap ability.  

Vlad revisits opinions from Kyambo “Hip Hop” Joshua and Elliott Wilson, framing the conversation as emcee versus artist: Jay-Z as the “rapper’s rapper” and Kanye as a boundary-pushing musical creator. The discussion also touches on Yankee Stadium performances, Kanye’s more conceptual live shows, and Hit-Boy’s run after “N****s in Paris” and “Clique.”  

An insightful VladTV conversation for fans searching Jay-Z, Kanye West, Hit-Boy, Beyoncé, hip-hop production, rap debates, and modern music legacy.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/U699JHhcvnM
--------

In this VladTV interview, Brian “Glaze” Gibbs reacts to Azie Faison’s harrowing account of a New York home invasion where masked gunmen forced him to open a safe, threatened his family, and shot him in the head. Gibbs says he knows the men connected to the attack, discussing figures from the 1980s crack era, including Fat Cat, “Puerto Rican Righteous,” and others tied to Queens and the Bronx violence. He also reflects on the informants, life sentences, and cooperation that followed.

Gibbs looks back on his own admitted murders from 1987–1988, explaining why today’s cameras, cell phones, drones, and federal surveillance make the old street life nearly impossible to survive. Now living free after 29 years out of prison, he talks regret, peace, work ethic, Colorado, his book, and a possible screenplay once involving LL Cool J. A raw conversation on crime, consequences, and change.

recentItems.description:

Part 1: https://youtu.be/JfU9hp8uTqY
--------
Charleston White sits down with VladTV to break down cooperation, street politics, and why he believes killers often become witnesses when facing life in prison. The conversation touches on Brian “Glaze” Gibbs, Lil Durk’s federal case, King Von’s legacy, Chicago rap violence, Atlanta, Los Angeles, New York, and the FBI’s scrutiny of rap crews tied to public feuds involving Quando Rondo, NBA YoungBoy, and 6ix9ine.

White also reacts to Trap Lore Ross reporting from outside Durk’s courtroom and fans confronting him, arguing that most people “pressing” media at a federal courthouse are performing for cameras—not risking real charges. He says Ross has the right to cover the trial as credentialed media and warns that assault near a federal court could bring serious consequences.

The discussion also references Durk’s rise, major collaborations with Drake and J. Cole, and how lyrics, loyalty, grief, and legal pressure can collide.
